retrieved_sources.title: The importance and challenges of observing social interactions in autistic preschoolers during inclusive educational settings: A scoping review

gioi_han: Preschool observation methods, not evidence that a named school programme works for every child.
Sparse longitudinal evidence; findings do not establish school services or rights in Vietnam.
Source/provenance review only; no independent clinical appraisal.
Retain actual ages, geography and study limitations; no individualized diagnosis, treatment or dosing inference.

retrieved_sources.title: Autism Spectrum Social Stories in Schools Trial 2 (ASSSIST‐2): a pragmatic randomised controlled trial of the Social Stories™ intervention to address the social and emotional health of autistic children in UK primary schools

gioi_han: Primary intention-to-treat social responsiveness outcome was not statistically significant; individual socio-emotional goals improved.
Do not claim global social-skill, anxiety, depression or caregiver-stress improvement from individual-goal findings.
Social Stories are not PEERS and this trial does not reproduce a licensed PEERS treatment manual.
No independent clinical review; research/internal noncommercial use, no individual diagnosis or prescription.

retrieved_sources.title: Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions: Empirically Validated Treatments for Autism Spectrum Disorder

source.ten_nguon: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

gioi_han: Foundational 2015 description of NDBIs, not a current professional practice guideline or a head-to-head trial.
Intervention choices and goals must be individualized; no guaranteed language gain, cure or fixed intensity for all children.
Reviews/program descriptions can overlap underlying studies; not independent replication.
No independent clinical review; research/internal noncommercial use, no individual diagnosis or prescription.

Linked 2022 commentary (PMC9561015) revisits simplification of adult language input; this foundational 2015 review is not a settled language-input prescription. The commentary link is not a retraction or correction notice.

retrieved_sources.title: Food Selectivity in Children with Autism: Guidelines for Assessment and Clinical Interventions

source.ten_nguon: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

gioi_han: A narrative clinical review with guidelines in its title is not an official society guideline.
Clinician-directed feeding procedures are not instructions for unsupervised family implementation.
Keep actual study ages; pediatric and mixed adult findings cannot be generalized to every age from birth to 18.
No independent clinical appraisal; no individualized treatment or dosing inference.
Title uses Guidelines but this is not a formal professional-society guideline.
Clinician-directed behavioral feeding procedures, physical guidance and escape extinction are not instructions for unsupervised family implementation.
Food selectivity does not by itself establish deficiency, food allergy or a need for restrictive diets.

retrieved_sources.title: A systematic review of ayres sensory integration intervention for children with autism

gioi_han: Ayres Sensory Integration (ASI) with fidelity and trained therapists is not equivalent to generic sensory-based activities or all occupational therapy.
Search covered 2006–2017; three studies met final criteria. CEC evidence classification is not a universal current clinical recommendation.

Predates SenITA 2022 (https://doi.org/10.3310/TQGE0020), which found no significant main benefit over usual care on its primary outcome; do not present the older positive conclusion as current consensus.
Do not infer effectiveness for infants, all cognitive profiles or every ASD outcome; no home pressure/weighted-device prescription.
No independent clinical review; research/internal noncommercial use, no individual diagnosis or prescription.
